name: Spokane & Coeur d'Alene
summary: A river-city and a jewel of a lake at the gateway to the northern Rockies — falls in the middle of downtown, and a resort town on the water.

lodging.name: A Coeur d'Alene lakefront resort
lodging.blurb: On the water, with a boardwalk.

foodMustTry.name: Huckleberry everything
foodMustTry.blurb: The wild berry of the Inland Northwest.

days.label: Day 520 — Lake & Falls
days.summary: The lake and the river city.

item.title: Coeur d'Alene Lake & Spokane Falls
item.blurb: The floating boardwalk and beaches of Lake Coeur d'Alene, plus Riverfront Park and the falls in downtown Spokane just west.

days.label: Day 521 — Down US-95
days.summary: Most of the length of Idaho, and an afternoon on a lake.

commute.scenicNote: South on US-95 — the only road that runs the length of Idaho — through the Palouse wheat country, down to the Snake at Lewiston, up the White Bird grade, and along the Salmon River into the mountains. Leave early and take the stops; this is the drive, not the gap between two of them.

stopsAlongWay.title: Hells Gate & the Lewis-Clark confluence, Lewiston
stopsAlongWay.blurb: Where the Clearwater meets the Snake at 730 feet — Idaho's only seaport, 465 river miles from the Pacific, and the jumping-off point for jetboats into Hells Canyon.

stopsAlongWay.title: The White Bird grade
stopsAlongWay.blurb: Pull off at the summit for the view down onto the old 1921 switchback road and the battlefield where the Nez Perce War began.

stopsAlongWay.title: Riggins
stopsAlongWay.blurb: Four hundred people wedged between the canyon walls where the Little Salmon meets the Salmon — the whitewater capital of Idaho, and the right place to stop for lunch.

rest.label: Afternoon on Payette Lake
rest.note: You'll be into McCall by mid-afternoon, which is the whole point of stopping here. Nothing is scheduled: the lake has a public beach three blocks off the main street, the water is cold, and the day ends better in it than in a car.
